Sardis, Church of
SAR-dis, CHURCH uhv
proper noun
One of the seven churches of Asia addressed in Revelation 2–3; Sardis, the ancient capital of Lydia.

📖 Biblical Definition

The church of Sardis was one of the seven churches of Asia to which the risen Christ sent letters through John in the Revelation, and it received the most solemn warning of all—the church with a reputation for life that was, in truth, dead. To Sardis the Lord said, I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead. Outwardly the church flourished, esteemed by men, with a name for vitality; inwardly it was a corpse, its works not found perfect before God, its spiritual life all but extinguished. The Lord’s charge was urgent: be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die; remember how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent. If thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief. Yet even in dead Sardis there was a remnant: thou hast a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments, and they shall walk with me in white, for they are worthy. The dictionary reads the church of Sardis as the abiding warning against dead orthodoxy and reputation without reality—the church that men praise and God indicts, alive in name and dead in fact—and as a call to watchfulness, repentance, and the strengthening of what remains; with the comfort that even in the deadest church God preserves His undefiled few, who shall walk with Christ in white.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

One of the seven churches of Revelation, with “a name that thou livest, and art dead”; the warning against dead orthodoxy, called to watch and repent, yet with a faithful few undefiled.

“Thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead” (Rev 3:1).

📖 Key Scripture

Rev 3:1 — "And unto the angel of the church in Sardis write; These things saith he that hath the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars; I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead."

Rev 3:2 — "Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die: for I have not found thy works perfect before God."

Rev 3:3 — "Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee."

Rev 3:4 — "Thou hast a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Sardis warns against the dead orthodoxy and reputation-without-reality that men praise and God indicts; the call is to watch, repent, and strengthen what remains.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption Sardis embodies is dead orthodoxy—a church with a name for life but no life, esteemed by men yet a corpse before God. It is a peril of sound churches especially: a congregation may keep the right doctrine, the old forms, the respected name, and the busy programs, while the Spirit has withdrawn and the works are found imperfect before God—outwardly alive, inwardly dead. The age that measures a church by its reputation, its size, or its heritage may praise a Sardis that God indicts; and the danger is the more deadly because it wears the appearance of health.

The principle to recover is watchfulness, repentance, and the strengthening of what remains. The risen Christ does not abandon dead Sardis but commands it to wake: be watchful, strengthen the things that remain and are ready to die, remember what you received, hold fast, and repent—or He will come as a thief. And He gives the comfort that even in the deadest church He preserves a faithful remnant: a few names that have not defiled their garments, who shall walk with Him in white. The lesson for every church is to seek not a name for life but life itself, in the reality of the Spirit’s presence and the fruit of true godliness, lest it be alive in name and dead in fact.
